def compact(inp, depth=0):
    out={k: inp.get(k) for k in ['name','label','type','value','argument','optional','multiple'] if k in inp}
    if 'options' in inp and isinstance(inp['options'], list):
        out['options']=[o for o in inp['options'][:20]]
    if 'cases' in inp:
        out['cases']=[{'value':c.get('value'),'inputs':[compact(x, depth+1) for x in c.get('inputs',[])]} for c in inp['cases'][:10]]
    if 'inputs' in inp and depth < 3:
        out['inputs']=[compact(x, depth+1) for x in inp['inputs']]
    return out
print(json.dumps({'id':t.get('id'),'version':t.get('version'),'inputs':[compact(i) for i in t.get('inputs',[])]}, indent=2)[:12000])

item.text: Because the seed input is comma-delimited CSV and Datamash operates on tabular fields, I’m adding a Galaxy format-conversion step first using Galaxy’s CSV-to-tabular converter.

from bioblend.galaxy import GalaxyInstance
with open(os.environ['GALAXY_API_KEY_FILE']) as f: key=f.read().strip()
gi=GalaxyInstance('https://usegalaxy.org', key=key)
for tool_id in ['csv_to_tabular','tabular_to_csv']:
 t=gi.tools.show_tool(tool_id, io_details=True)
 def compact(inp, depth=0):
  out={k:inp.get(k) for k in ['name','label','type','value','argument','optional','multiple'] if k in inp}
  if 'options' in inp and isinstance(inp['options'], list): out['options']=inp['options'][:20]
  if 'inputs' in inp and depth<3: out['inputs']=[compact(x,depth+1) for x in inp['inputs']]
  if 'cases' in inp: out['cases']=[{'value':c.get('value'),'inputs':[compact(x,depth+1) for x in c.get('inputs',[])]} for c in inp['cases']]
  return out
 print(json.dumps({'id':t.get('id'),'version':t.get('version'),'inputs':[compact(i) for i in t.get('inputs',[])]}, indent=2))
PY"
